binders: Real-valued pressure p(x,t) and velocity u(x,t).
Real K (bulk modulus), rho (density), x, and t.
conclusions: At (x,t), the vector equation q_t+A q_x=0 with q=(p,u) and A=[[0,K],[1/rho,0]] holds, including existence of the vector derivatives, if and only if the scalar component equations p_t+K*u_x=0 and u_t+(1/rho)*p_x=0 hold, including existence of all four component derivatives.
mathematical_definitions: q(x,t)=(p(x,t),u(x,t)) as a Fin 2-indexed real vector.
A has first row (0,K) and second row (rho^(-1),0).
Both sides are pointwise predicates using one-variable derivatives with the other coordinate fixed.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For arbitrary real pressure and velocity fields, parameters K and nonzero rho, and a point (x,t), the two-component conservation law q_t+A q_x=0 for q=(p,u) and A=[[0,K],[1/rho,0]] is logically equivalent to the pair of scalar equations p_t+K u_x=0 and u_t+(1/rho)p_x=0, with the relevant pointwise derivatives required to exist on each side.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: K is an arbitrary real number; no positivity assumption is encoded.
rho is required only to be nonzero, not positive.
The statement is local to one arbitrary point (x,t), although all x,t are universally quantified.

Each side explicitly includes existence of its own derivative witnesses; the equivalence therefore also asserts correspondence between differentiability of the bundled vector and differentiability of its components.
No claim of global solution existence, uniqueness, initial/boundary conditions, or hyperbolicity is encoded.
Real reciprocal is totalized, but rho != 0 ensures ordinary division.
